0|2d1af6a11cb9d88e0e3dd10258904c437fe1b315|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"drm/amdgpu: Don't fail resume process if resuming atomic state fails
This is an ugly one unfortunately. Currently
atomic modesetting will save the state that userspace had set before
suspending
column2: then attempt to restore that state on resume. This probably

column1: worked very well at one point
into the picture. While it's easy to restore state on normal display
connectors that were disconnected during suspend regardless of their
state post-resume
column2: this can't really be done with MST because of the

column1: fact that setting up a downstream sink requires performing sideband
transactions between the source and the MST hub
packets
Because of this
column2: there isn't really a guarantee that we can restore the

column1: atomic state we had before suspend once we've resumed. This sucks pretty
bad
column2: but so far I haven't run into any compositors that this actually

column1: causes serious issues with. Most compositors will notice the hotplug we
send afterwards
Since nouveau and i915 also don't fail the suspend/resume process due to
failing to restore the atomic state
behavior. Better to resume the GPU properly
half way because of a potentially unavoidable atomic commit failure.
Eventually
column2: we'll have a real fix for this problem on the DRM level. But

column1: we've got some more important low-hanging fruit to deal with first.
